Google News plus named outlets (TechCrunch, Forbes, Bloomberg, Reuters, VentureBeat, Wired, Business Insider, The Verge, Axios)

Review platforms (G2, Capterra, Trustpilot, Google Reviews, Gartner Peer Insights, Glassdoor, Clutch, TrustRadius, app stores)
Social (LinkedIn posts/profiles/exec posts, X, Reddit, YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, TikTok)

SEC EDGAR, UK Companies House, EU TED procurement awards
Crunchbase funding data, podcasts, GitHub releases, Product Hunt, Google Patents

newsletter_capability_detail: Newsletter coverage is already a named, sold feature, not a gap. The data-sources page lists 'Industry newsletters and trade press' as a news source type, and separately a custom/private source called 'Newsletter content' described as 'A competitor's own email newsletter, forwarded or subscribed.' The pricing page lists 'News & content — Google News, newsletters, blogs' as an included channel and 'Google News + newsletters' in the plan matrix. Coverage is per tracked company (10–100 companies), not a searchable publication corpus.

350+ sources across 62 source types is the platform total.

likely_buyer_role: Founder (Naveed Ratansi) — sole decision-maker in a founder-led, self-serve product

contact_route.value: Naveed Ratansi, Founder — contact form / 30-min call booking; no email published

caveats: Do not pitch newsletter coverage as missing - they already sell it. The real opening is breadth and structure: their newsletter coverage is per-competitor (a company's own email plus generic trade press), not an index of 26,401 publications with sponsor and guest relationships. Volume is small (10-100 tracked companies, £149/month), so an enterprise data licence would need a specific, cheap use case. Naveed is both buyer and contact, and he vets claims hard (the page publishes rejected claims and a 29-check pipeline), so evidence quality matters more than framing.
